question.worked_solution:
First, we write $1\,\frac{2}{3}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{2}{3}=\frac{(1\times 3)+2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}
$$

We also write  $2\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(2\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{9}{4}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}\times \frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}\times \frac{9}{4} & =\frac{5}{4}\times \frac{9}{3} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\times 3 \\  & =\frac{15}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{15}{4}=3\,\text{R}3=3\,\frac{3}{4}
$$
